what_happened: Reproduced the git-commit-scoped.sh silent-staging-drop symptom (named positive pathspec absent from a successful exit-0 commit) in a controlled scratch-repo harness: two concurrent invocations naming the same shared path, with the specs/.commit-lock mutex forced into its own documented fail-open path (pre-occupied by a long-lived foreign holder), reproduced the drop in 1/10 and 3/20 trials; a control run with the mutex working normally showed 0/20 drops across two batches. This pins the mechanism to the mutex's fail-open branch plus a genuinely concurrent second writer on the same path, directly falsifying that branch's own in-code safety comment.

Research recommendation 1 specified the post-commit integrity snapshot as 'git hash-object against the working-tree file' per pathspec, which only works for a pathspec naming exactly one regular file; it cannot handle a directory pathspec (specs/{NNN}_{slug}/, which real callers pass and the suite's U6/W4 cases exercise), a glob, or :(exclude) interaction. The plan diverges by keeping the hash-comparison semantics but letting git's own pathspec resolver enumerate the intended file set, and states the divergence explicitly in Research Integration.

The research report ruled out three of four candidate mechanisms by direct code reading and supplied the load-bearing git-semantics fact (git commit -- pathspec re-reads the working tree at commit time), so planning needed no second research round and could ground every phase's file targets and verification in the script's actual control flow.

Phase 1: the primary candidate injection (a planted pre-commit hook mutating the temporary partial index GIT_INDEX_FILE points at during 'git commit -- <pathspec>') reproduced the exact incident shape deterministically on the first attempt -- 100% reproduction, confirmed by a direct GIT_INDEX_FILE/git-update-index probe before writing assertions. The research's probabilistic two-writer forced-fail-open harness (3/20, 1/10 trials) was therefore not needed as a fallback and was not ported into the default suite; this is recorded as a deliberate Phase 1 scope decision, not an omission.
